correctness.rationale: PASS: Nonalgebraic complete 1-types over finite induced parameter poset P in the homogeneous random poset correspond bijectively to admissible (lower ideal D, upper filter U) one-point extensions satisfying D<U. For Q=P+v, any restriction fiber has <=3 placements (below/above/incomparable v), and exactly one existing P-profile (D,U)=(L,H) has all three. If P contains a comparable pair there is also a distinct singleton fiber: choose x above all P when v lies below some old point, below all P when v lies above some, or between a<b when v is incomparable to all P. Hence total t(Q)<=2t(P). Start from an induced C2 with t=6, append n-2 arbitrary points to get t(P)<=6*2^(n-2)=3*2^(n-1). Antichain profiles give 2^(n+1)-1. One disjoint chain plus isolated vertices and height-two star/dual attain equality. Independently enumerated every labeled strict partial order through n=5 (1,3,19,219,4231 cases n=1..5), checked all legal profiles and sharpness counts; infinite proof is the restriction-fiber lemma.
